study.title: The Status of the Quality Control in Acupuncture-Neuroimaging Studies
study.study_design: Systematic review / bibliometric analysis of original acupuncture-neuroimaging articles published in English from 1995 to 2014 on PubMed
study.population: Original acupuncture-neuroimaging studies performed on human beings
study.disease_condition: Multiple; includes healthy volunteers and patients with neurological, pain, psychosomatic, gastroenterological, pediatric, rheumatological, dermatological, and ophthalmological conditions
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) original articles; (2) acupuncture-neuroimaging studies on human beings; (3) published in English; and (4) published during 1995 to 2014
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) reviews or editorials or trial protocols; (2) acupuncture-neuroimaging studies on animals; or (3) duplicate articles

extraction_notes.note: This is a review article / bibliometric analysis of 168 included studies. It does not present original neuroimaging data, coordinates, or clinical trial results. All extracted values are aggregate characteristics of the 168 included studies, not primary experimental results.

No original neuroimaging coordinates, peak statistics, cluster sizes, or threshold information are reported. The neuroimaging methods section is populated with descriptive information about technologies used across included studies, not from a single study protocol.
No individual participant-level data, effect sizes, or inter-study statistical comparisons are reported. All outcomes are frequency counts or proportions across the 168 included studies.

Sham acupuncture and placebo control details are referenced only in a descriptive sense (e.g., sham acupoint vs. real acupoint), without extraction of any specific sham procedure details from included studies.

Deqi / needle sensation data are reported only as counts of how many studies required or measured Deqi, and which scales were used. No quantitative deqi values from any included study are presented in this review.

Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success data are not assessed or reported in this review article. Only emotional state (anxiety/depression scales) used in a subset of 4 included studies is mentioned.
Adverse events are not discussed or reported in this review.

The proportion '63.7%' stated for international cooperation (60 studies) appears inconsistent if taken as a proportion of 168 studies (60/168 = 35.7%). The paper states '63.7% of the studies were accomplished by the cooperation of more than two countries' in the Discussion, but in the Results states '60 studies'. These numbers are inconsistent and may refer to different denominators or contain a typographical error. Both values have been preserved as reported.

Figure 4 shows bar chart values for needle sensation scales: VAS=41, MASS=5, MASS and VAS=3, SASS=3, 6-point Likert scale=1, Park questionnaire=1, PRNS=1, NSQ=1. The total is 56, consistent with the text stating '56 studies evaluated needle sensation.' The 68.3% VAS usage figure (41/56 rounded) is consistent.
The paper states '100 studies described the age range' in one paragraph and later '101 studies' in the Discussion. The extraction uses '100 studies' as stated in the Results section (section 3.2.2).
The article is published in Evidence-Based Complementary and Alternative Medicine, Volume 2016, Article ID 3685785. The PMID is not visible in the PDF text and has been marked as not_reported.
